packageRules.description: One pull request per pin. A batched bump is a batched revert, and these pins fail in unrelated ways — a CloudNativePG minor and a mermaid patch have nothing to say to each other.

Label the pins this repository maintains deliberately, so they stay findable. config:recommended also proposes npm and GitHub Actions majors — fifteen of them on the first run — and the versions.env pins are the ones that have actually broken things: MinIO vanishing from Docker Hub, and appVersion four releases behind its own chart.

MinIO's tags are RELEASE.<timestamp>, which `loose` versioning cannot parse — it skipped both pins with skipReason invalid-value, so Renovate could never have proposed a bump for the one dependency that has already broken CI by disappearing. A regex versioning reads the date as major.minor.patch and the time as the build, which orders correctly. It also does the filtering allowedVersions used to attempt: the pattern requires a trailing Z, so the -cpuv1 and .hotfix. variants do not parse and are ignored rather than mistaken for newer.

The API image this chart deploys is built from this repository, so a bump here is the promotion step decision 0002 says has to be a second merge. It cannot be automerged: the commit being released cannot name the image the release is about to build.

customManagers.description: scripts/versions.env is a bespoke file, so each pin names its own datasource. The comment above each is the reason it is pinned; this is only the address it is pinned to.

The chart's appVersion IS the API image tag when image.tag is unset, which is the default and the documented path. It sat four releases behind once and a default install could not become ready (#119).
The PostgreSQL image every hosted database runs. A major here is a PostgreSQL major for every customer, so it is never a quiet bump.
